title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Throughout, J is a 3-element set. The page builds, without choosing coordinates, the projective line attached to J together with its S_3 = Aut(J)-symmetric special points. This is the coordinate-free model of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity} = M_{0,4} with the action of the symmetric group S_3, which is the base level of the Teichmüller tower studied in this folder.

(1) The line Sigma_J. V(J) is the kernel of the sum map O^J -> O, a rank-2 module. Sigma_J = P(V(J)), in Grothendieck's convention where P(V) parametrises rank-1 quotients. In rank 2 there is a canonical isomorphism P(V) = P-check(V), coming from V = V* (x) det V. The tautological sequence is 0 -> F -> V(J)_Sigma -> O_Sigma(1) -> 0.

(2) Twists. Let omega = omega(J) be the 2-element torsor of cyclic orientations of J; det V(J) is the line twisted by omega. Since F has rank 1, F (x) O(1) = det V(J), so F(1) = O(omega). The marginal note describes the pairing F x V(J) -> det V(J) given by exterior product. The Euler sequence then gives Omega^1 = F(-1) = O(-2)(omega) and tangent bundle O(2)(omega). Here omega^{-1} = omega, because det V(J)^{(x)2} is canonically trivial. Sign conventions are explicitly flagged ('attention signes!').

(3) The points R_i, i in J (the 'holes'). For J = {i,j,k}, R_i is the quotient of V(J) that kills e_j - e_k. In V(J)/R_i one has e_i - e_j = e_i - e_k, so the fibre O(1)_{R_i} is canonically trivial; R-tilde_i is the distinguished point above R_i. Global sections are Gamma(Sigma, O(1)) = V(J). The sections phi_{jk} = e_k - e_j satisfy:
- phi_{kj} = -phi_{jk};
- the cocycle relation phi_{ij} + phi_{jk} + phi_{ki} = 0;
- phi_{jk} vanishes at R_i;
- phi_{jk}(R_k) = R-tilde_k and phi_{jk}(R_j) = -R-tilde_j.
These are the three cusps 0, 1, infinity.

(4) The points Q_i. Q_i is the quotient killing -2e_i + e_j + e_k. There the image of e_j - e_k is defined only up to orientation, so O(1)_{Q_i} = O(omega). Its two privileged points, indexed by omega, are Q-tilde_i = phi_{jk}(Q_i) and Q-tilde'_i = phi_{kj}(Q_i). The box Q_i^omega = phi_{omega i, omega^2 i}(Q_i) uses an orientation omega to name them, with Q_i^{omega^{-1}} = -Q_i^omega. In coordinates the Q_i are 1/2, 2, -1: together with R_i they are the fixed points of the transposition fixing i. They are the elliptic points of order 2 (j = 1728) and the midpoints of the edges R_j R_k of the triangle map.

(5) The points P_omega and P_{i,omega}. P_omega, omega in omega(J), are introduced next with a chosen primitive cube root zeta = exp(2 pi i/3). They are the two fixed points of the 3-cycles, -zeta and -zeta^2, i.e. the order-3 elliptic points (j = 0) and the face centres of the triangle map. P_{i,omega} are presumably further points of the barycentric subdivision. The page breaks off at 'Alors'.

Purpose. This is the S_3-equivariant 'carte' (dessin) on P^1: vertices R_i, edge midpoints Q_i, face centres P_omega. The next page treats exactly such regular maps of polygons and their dihedral coverings of P^1 - {0, infinity, 1, -1} and of U_{0,3}.
errors: No mathematical errors found. Checked: F(1) = det V (rank-1 F); Omega^1 = O(-2) (x) det V; phi_{jk}(R_k) = +R-tilde_k and phi_{jk}(R_j) = -R-tilde_j agree with the stated convention; the cocycle relation holds.
The tangent bundle written O(2)(omega) rather than O(2)(omega^{-1}) is harmless, since omega^{(x)2} is canonically trivial.
The marginal formula for the pairing F x V(J) -> O is partly garbled and cannot be checked in detail.

ideas.what: Canonical projective line P(V(J)) attached to a 3-element set J, with V(J) = ker(sum), and its automatic S_3-equivariance
ideas.modern_name: Coordinate-free model of M_{0,4} = P^1 - {0,1,inf} with its S_3-action
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (cross-ratio, anharmonic group); Grothendieck/Drinfeld/Ihara for the Teichmüller-tower framing
ideas.where_published: M_{0,4} and its S_3 symmetry are discussed in Esquisse d'un programme; this specific linear-algebra model is not known to be published

ideas.what: Twisting by the orientation torsor omega(J) = det V(J); Omega^1 = O(-2)(omega); sign bookkeeping
ideas.modern_name: Euler sequence with determinant twist; sign character of S_3
ideas.where_published: EGA II section 4 / SGA (projective bundles, Euler sequence)

ideas.what: Distinguished points: cusps R_i with canonically trivialised fibres, sections phi_{jk} with cocycle relation; points Q_i (order-2 fixed points) and P_omega (order-3 fixed points, needing zeta)
ideas.modern_name: Elliptic points j = 1728 and j = 0 / vertices, edge midpoints and face centres of the triangle dessin (barycentric subdivision)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses M_{0,4}, its points with extra automorphisms and tangential base points, but not in this form

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful, coordinate-free, sign-conscious set-up of the S_3-symmetric P^1 with its cusps and elliptic points. It is preparatory bookkeeping for the dessin and Teichmüller-tower computations, and everything on the page is classical or standard.
transcription_corrections: 'R_i = V(J)' is likely 'R_i in P(V(J))' (a point given by a quotient of V(J)); similarly 'Q_i in P(V(J))'.
Read 'O_k(e_k - e_j)' as the line generated by e_k - e_j, i.e. the kernel defining R_i.
Read 'fibré tangent de Sigma' as the label for Omega-check^1.
The marginal box reads roughly 'abs: Q_i^{omega^{-1}} = -Q_i^omega', together with 'phi_{omega i, omega^2 i}(Q_i) = Q_i^omega'.
'les deux points privilégiés de O(omega)*_{Q_i} indexés par omega sont notés Q-tilde_i, Q-tilde'_i, ou Q_{i,omega} ((i,omega) in J x omega)'.
